gen.title: Increasing wing area to keep lift high at low velocity
gen.orderNote: Follows page order from cruise baseline through low velocity need to flap and slat deployment.

steps.label: cruise condition
steps.quote: The airplane on the left is shown in a cruise condition while the airplane on the right is shown in a takeoff or landing condition.
steps.orderHint: Follow wing area growth from cruise to takeoff and landing.

steps.label: relatively low velocity
steps.quote: Takeoff and landing are times of relatively low velocity, so to keep the lift high (to avoid the ground!) designers try to increase the wing area.
steps.orderHint: Follow wing area growth from cruise to takeoff and landing.

steps.label: sliding the flaps backwards
steps.quote: This is done by sliding the flaps backwards along metal tracks
steps.orderHint: Follow wing area growth from cruise to takeoff and landing.

steps.label: shifting the slats forward
steps.quote: shifting the slats forward to increase the wing area.
steps.orderHint: Follow wing area growth from cruise to takeoff and landing.

steps.label: change in wing area
steps.quote: watch the wings during takeoff and landing to see the change in wing area.
steps.orderHint: Follow wing area growth from cruise to takeoff and landing.
